slides.title: Perfect Forwarding Problem & Solution
slides.prompt: Perfect forwarding allows wrapper functions to pass arguments to target functions while preserving their exact value categories (lvalueness or rvalueness). This is achieved using forwarding references (T&&) and std::forward<T>.

slides.title: Difference Between std::move and std::forward
slides.prompt: How does std::forward<T> differ fundamentally from std::move?
options: std::move unconditionally casts to rvalue; std::forward conditionally casts to rvalue only if its template argument T was deduced as rvalue
std::forward executes faster at runtime than std::move
std::move requires template arguments; std::forward does not
std::forward creates deep copies while std::move does not
slides.correctAnswer: std::move unconditionally casts to rvalue; std::forward conditionally casts to rvalue only if its template argument T was deduced as rvalue

slides.title: Why Name of Forwarding Parameter is Lvalue
slides.prompt: Inside 'template<typename T> void logAndPass(T&& arg)', why is 'arg' treated as an lvalue inside logAndPass function body even when initialized with an rvalue?
options: Because 'arg' is a named variable, and all named variables are lvalue expressions
Because T&& automatically converts to a raw pointer
Because function scope locks rvalue memory
slides.correctAnswer: Because 'arg' is a named variable, and all named variables are lvalue expressions

slides.title: std::make_unique Internal Forwarding
slides.prompt: How does factory function std::make_unique<T>(args...) pass its arguments to the constructor of T?
options: Uses variadic template perfect forwarding with std::forward<Args>(args)...
Uses std::move on every parameter unconditionally
Passes all parameters by const reference
Copies arguments into a temporary tuple
slides.correctAnswer: Uses variadic template perfect forwarding with std::forward<Args>(args)...

slides.title: Consequence of Forgetting std::forward in Wrapper
slides.prompt: What happens if a wrapper function accepts T&& arg but passes 'arg' directly to targetFunction(arg) without std::forward?
options: The target function will always receive 'arg' as an lvalue, forcing copy overloads instead of move overloads
Compilation failure due to missing type qualifiers
slides.correctAnswer: The target function will always receive 'arg' as an lvalue, forcing copy overloads instead of move overloads
